references.text: Joseph's interpretation of the cupbearer's dream uses the expression 'lift up your head' positively (restoration), in contrast to 40:19 where 'lift your head from you' means execution.
The fulfillment of Joseph's interpretation: the cupbearer was restored and the baker was hanged, just as Joseph had predicted.
The law that whoever is hanged on a tree is cursed by God – the same motif found in Joseph's interpretation where the baker is to be hanged on a tree.
Goliath threatens that birds will eat David's flesh, the same motif as in Joseph's interpretation where birds are to eat the baker's flesh from his body.
The Philistines fastened Saul's body to the wall of Beth-Shan – a parallel to public desecration of corpses after execution.
Joseph's interpretation came true: the chief baker was hanged, just as Joseph had interpreted the dream.
The connection lies in the biblical motif where 'birds eating corpses' serves as a powerful image of total defeat and God's judgment.
This is a theological contrast where 'three days' marks execution in the Old Testament, but resurrection in the New.
The reference highlights how Jesus' resurrection on the 'third day' fulfills and transforms the old image of death after three days.
The contrast between execution after three days and resurrection on the third day underscores Jesus' victory over death.
The connection lies in the motif of a king or leader being stripped of human dignity and handed over to the world of beasts as judgment.
This is a clear thematic parallel where 'birds eating corpses' is a repeated image of God's complete judgment upon enemies.
